summary: The exact candidate implements the original issue's explicitly acceptable fail-fast resolution. Normal server resolution now rejects DFLASH with either PD role before scheduler/worker startup and gives an actionable explanation. It does not implement DFLASH draft-state transfer.

All 13 selected existing PD argument-handler tests passed at the exact candidate commit.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 was visible, but the candidate is a deterministic Python argument-validation change and no GPU result is claimed.

remaining_counterexamples: The special model_path values dummy and none return from the resolution pipeline before handle_pd_disaggregation, so synthetic DFLASH+PD records are accepted. This path does not instantiate the reported DFLASH serving workload.
A DFLASH spelling with trailing whitespace misses this guard but is rejected later as an unknown speculative algorithm.
remaining_limitations: The candidate rejects unsupported DFLASH PD configurations; it does not transfer or rebuild DFLASH draft KV or auxiliary hidden states.
The reported Kimi-K3/Kimi-K3-DFlash weights were unavailable.
The reported 8x RTX 6000D sm_120 multi-node environment and MoonCake RDMA transport were unavailable.
No full-model, NVIDIA, multi-node, RDMA, semantic-accuracy, or performance execution was performed.
The available GPU was a single AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 under ROCm 7.2; it was not relevant to the CPU-side validation change.
